name: CDM collateral prototype
description: Local prototype architecture for CDM-based initial-margin management with tokenized collateral on Hyperledger Besu.

nodes.name: Pledgor operations
nodes.description: User acting for the party that posts initial margin: responds to margin calls (agree, partially agree, dispute) and approves returns.

nodes.name: Market data operator
nodes.description: Simulation user who changes mock NAV, prices and ratings to trigger revaluation and top-up calls.

nodes.name: Party console
nodes.description: Browser UI that drives the flows. One instance per participant, part of its participant stack (party identity, role and wallet set by configuration); it talks only to its own participant's services.

metadata.instances: N, one per participant; configured by PARTY_ID, ROLE and WALLET

nodes.name: End-to-end test harness
nodes.description: Test-only. Starts the stack, drives N party-console instances in parallel browser contexts with Playwright and asserts each CALM flow end to end, including on-chain state.

metadata.scope: test only, not part of the runtime

nodes.name: Secured party operations
nodes.description: User acting for the party that receives initial margin: issues margin calls, approves returns, declares a default and requests enforcement.

nodes.name: Windows developer machine
nodes.description: The developer's Windows machine. Python and Node.js services run natively or in WSL2; Besu runs in Docker Desktop (WSL2 backend).

nodes.name: Participant stack
nodes.description: Per-participant deployment (ADR wp-adr-per-participant-services): each simulated participant runs its own party console, collateral workflow service, workflow store, ledger gateway and keystore, holding only its own books and its own signing key, and connected to its own Besu validator node. N stacks run side by side; the oracle service, mock market data and contracts are shared.

metadata.instances: N, one per participant (pledgor, secured party, market operator)
metadata.isolation: own process, own SQLite file, own key; no shared database

nodes.name: CDM collateral prototype
nodes.description: Prototype that illustrates CDM-based initial-margin management with tokenized collateral segregated by a smart contract on a local Besu network. Nothing is deployed outside the developer machine.

nodes.name: Collateral workflow service
nodes.description: Off-chain margin workflow (ASR concept-asr-offchain-dispute), one instance per participant: holds that party's CDM agreements (ISDA IM CSA / CTA-SA elections, eligibility schedule), checks eligibility and haircuts with CDM functions, runs the margin call lifecycle (issue, respond, dispute) that CDM 7.6.0 does not provide (finding F2), exchanges margin calls, responses, return requests and default notices with the counterparty's instance, and sends its own party's movement instructions to its ledger gateway.

metadata.cdm-binding: CDM 7.6.0 Python distribution (assumption: availability to be confirmed)

nodes.name: CDM 7.6.0 object model
nodes.description: FINOS Common Domain Model release 7.6.0 (commit f685b4b) as the canonical data layer (ASR concept-asr-cdm-data-layer): LegalAgreement with CSA IM / CTA elections, EligibleCollateralSpecification, MarginCallIssuance / MarginCallResponse, CollateralPortfolio. Extended locally with on-chain asset identity (ASR concept-asr-onchain-asset-identity, finding B1).

nodes.name: Workflow store
nodes.description: One SQLite file per participant holding that party's agreements, margin calls and responses, disputes, movement instructions, collateral balances and the asset registry that maps ISIN/CUSIP and DTI to network and token contract.

nodes.name: Oracle service
nodes.description: Off-chain oracle endpoints, shared, run by the market data operator. Reads price / NAV and rating data from the mock market data source, serves it to every participant's collateral service for valuation and eligibility, and publishes signed updates on-chain through the operator's ledger gateway. Also relays a default notice from the secured party to the on-chain default feed.

nodes.name: Mock market data source
nodes.description: Local JSON files standing in for NAV, price and rating providers (in the GDF/ISDA sandbox: Kaiko, Redstone, Moody's).

nodes.name: Ledger gateway
nodes.description: Ledger-neutral interface (ASR concept-asr-ledger-neutrality, ADR wp-adr-prototype-ledgers): one instance per participant: accepts its participant's movement instructions (and, for the operator, oracle updates), signs with that participant's key only and submits transactions to the ledger, waits for finality and reports ledger events back to the collateral service. Besu adapter first; a Canton adapter is the second target.

nodes.name: Development keystore
nodes.description: Per participant: the private key of that participant's test account only (pledgor, secured party, or for the market operator the oracle publisher and contract admin keys). Development keys only.

nodes.name: Besu local network
nodes.description: Hyperledger Besu network in Docker Compose with QBFT consensus: four validator nodes, one per default participant (market operator, BANK-A, BANK-B, BANK-C), each participant's gateway connected to its own node (ADR wp-adr-per-participant-services). Deterministic finality per block (ASR concept-asr-settlement-finality); blocks continue with one node down. Stands in for a permissioned network such as DTCC's private Besu network.

metadata.consensus: QBFT, four validators, one node per participant

nodes.name: Tokenized collateral contracts
nodes.description: ERC-20 test tokens with transfer restrictions standing in for a tokenized money market fund and a tokenized US Treasury. Each token records its ISIN/CUSIP and DTI as metadata (ASR concept-asr-onchain-asset-identity).

nodes.name: Collateral control contract
nodes.description: Smart contract that holds pledged initial margin (ADR wp-adr-im-segregation). States per pledge: pledged, returned, enforced. Pledge: pledgor transfers tokens in. Return: needs approval by both parties or by the secured party. Enforce: secured party only, after the default feed reports a default. No other movement is possible.

nodes.name: Oracle feed contract
nodes.description: On-chain store of the latest price / NAV, rating and default status per asset and counterparty, written only by the oracle publisher account and read by the collateral control contract.

flows.name: Initial margin call and on-chain pledge
flows.description: The secured party calls initial margin; the pledgor agrees in full or in part off-chain; the pledgor pledges the agreed amount into the collateral control contract on Besu. Each party's stack keeps its own record.

transitions.description: Secured party issues an IM call (CDM MarginCallIssuance) under the agreement in its console.
Secured party console submits the call to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service sends the call to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor responds in its console: agree, partially agree or dispute (CDM MarginCallResponse); a disputed part stays off-chain.
Pledgor console submits the response and the proposed tokens to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor's service fetches NAV / prices and ratings for the proposed tokens.
Pledgor's service checks eligibility and haircuts against the CDM eligibility schedule and records the movement instruction in its own store.
Pledgor's service sends the response to the secured party's service, which records it in its own store.
Pledgor's service sends a pledge instruction for the agreed amount to the pledgor's gateway.
Pledgor's gateway signs with the pledgor key and submits pledge() to the collateral control contract.
Contract pulls the tokens from the pledgor's account.
Both parties' gateways receive the Pledged event in a finalized block.
Each gateway reports the event to its own workflow service, which updates its balance and closes the call.
Both consoles show the settled pledge and the new balance.

flows.name: Oracle price and rating update
flows.description: The oracle service publishes current NAV / price and rating data to the on-chain feed through the market operator's gateway.

transitions.description: Oracle reads mock NAV, price and rating data.
Oracle sends a signed update to the market operator's gateway.
Operator's gateway writes the update to the oracle feed contract with the oracle publisher key.

flows.name: Collateral revaluation and top-up call
flows.description: The market operator lowers the NAV or price of a pledged token; the secured party's revaluation shows a shortfall and it issues a top-up call, which then follows the IM call flow.

transitions.description: Market operator changes the NAV or price of a token.
Operator console sends the new mock value.
Oracle updates the mock market data.
Oracle publishes the new value on-chain.
Secured party's workflow service revalues pledged collateral after haircuts.
Secured party console shows the shortfall and the proposed top-up call.

flows.name: Return of initial margin
flows.description: Excess or released initial margin goes back to the pledgor after the secured party's approval, which the secured party signs on-chain.

transitions.description: Pledgor requests a return in its console.
Pledgor console submits the request to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor's service sends the return request to the secured party's service.
Secured party approves the return in its console.
Secured party console submits the approval to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service sends the return approval to the secured party's gateway.
Secured party's gateway signs with the secured party key and submits returnPledge().
Contract transfers the tokens back to the pledgor.
Each gateway reports the Returned event to its own workflow service, which records the return and updates its balance.

flows.name: Default and enforcement
flows.description: After a pledgor default, the secured party enforces against the pledged initial margin.

transitions.description: Secured party declares a pledgor default in its console.
Console submits the default declaration to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service sends the default notice to the pledgor's service.
Secured party's service forwards the default notice to the oracle service.
Oracle publishes the default status through the operator's gateway.
Operator's gateway writes the default to the feed; the secured party's gateway then submits enforce() with the secured party key.
Contract confirms the default status.
Contract transfers the pledged tokens to the secured party.
Each gateway reports the Enforced event to its own workflow service, which records the enforcement.
